recipes.name: Cheater Baked Ziti
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package shredded Italian cheese blend

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a boil. Stir in the ziti, and return to a boil. Cook the pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through but is still slightly firm, about 12 minutes. Drain well.

While the pasta is cooking, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in the sausage. Cook and stir until the sausage is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Stir in the pasta, spaghetti sauce, and Alfredo sauce. Transfer the mixture into a large baking dish, and top with the Italian cheese blend.
Bake in the preheated oven until the sauce is bubbly and the cheese is melted, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheater Baked Ziti
raw_recipe.description: Creamy store-bought Alfredo sauce replaces the usual ricotta cheese in this spicy pasta dish. For less heat, skip the hot sausage and use mild Italian sausage instead.

video.description: Baked ziti is so much easier when you use jars of pasta sauce! Bake this cheesy pasta until it's bubbly for a simple weeknight dinner!

review.reviewBody: A triumph for lazy people everywhere!
Great recipe! Cheat, quick and delicious! I only had ground beef on hand and it was still amazing.
Easy and Delicious. I added sliced turkey pepperoni (half a bag) to the mix and it added a nice texture as well as flavor to it. Loved this!

Very good recipe! I subbed sweet Italian sausage. The day I made it was 90* and I didn’t want to warm up the house, so I finished on grill uncovered for 25 minutes at 350*. I used extra cheese and a pellet grill so that’s why it took longer than recipe. Very good subtle smoky flavor! Probably will make it the same way again.

Made this last night, just as written - no changes. Used roasted garlic alfredo and a veggie-based spaghetti sauce. I found it very tasty, the boyfriend also enjoyed it, and co-workers rated it as "awesome". This was easy, quick and cost-effective!! Thanks!!

Easy weekday dinner. My family loves pasta so when I found this recipe, I knew we needed to try it. Can't praise this recipe enough for ease - few ingredients, quick prep, and great flavor. The only change made was using the mild italian sausage just to cut back on it being too spicy. I loved being able to make this and have dinner ready in under 40 minutes tops. Bonus - the leftovers are even better b/c the flavors really meld together.

This is so easy! I cheated even more and used homemade sauce that already had lots of mild italian sausage in it. I cooked the pasta and than stirred in the jarred Alfredo sauce to coat the noodles - put half of the noodles in a greased baking dish, did a layer of sauce and then some cheese - the rest of the noodles, more sauce and cover the top with cheese. Baked covered with foil so it wouldn't dry out - remove the foil and baked for another 10 - 15 minutes. The kids loved it.

For someone who works all the time- I really love easy dishes that are also good on a budget- this ziti was perfect, and it made so much! Before I baked it I devided the ziti mixture to 2 smaller casserole dishes so I could freeze one for later. Also, because I had precooked veggies from another dinner, I threw those into the dish- didn't change the flavor and my picky family ate everything!! Great recepi!

I followed the recipe except used ground beef. When browning the meat, I added minced garlic, basil, oregano, dried minced onion, salt & pepper to give the meat some flavor. The flavor from mixing the sauces was so good!! I also mix in the cheese to the sauce blend instead of put on top. Was a big hit with the family!

I loved it! I was skeptical at first with combining Alfredo and marinara sauce together, but it turned out great. I did add pepper, garlic and onion powder, basil, oregano, fennel and onions. I only had Italian and sage sausage. I also had only Parmesan, mozzarella, and pepper jack cheese. Used all 3. This meal was easy to prepare, filling, and delicious. Thanks!
So good. I make it even easier by not boiling the ziti. I just stir in the dry noodles and 1 cup of water.

Outstanding! Easy to make and delicious! Even my picky grands love this one! It is great for company, too. I serve this with a salad or asparagus, and garlic bread. The sides take longer to make than the dish! Definitely a keeper!

I've been making this recipe for years and we've loved it! We've called it "pink sauce" and have used gluten free rotini. Can't go wrong with whatever modifications you want to add to it. I love adding black olives now & then and the kids can't get enough cheese.

Making this as directed for the 4th time tonight - the entire family goes back for seconds so I double the recipe so we can enjoy left overs for lunch too. I use the Publix brand hot Italian sausage, prego Italian sausage and garlic meat sauce and Bertolli 4 cheese alfredo sauce. I top with sargentos 6 cheese Italian blend. I also used Rigatoni noodles the first time we made it because I couldn’t find ziti so we have stuck with rigatoni noodles. It’s so tasty and creamy most importantly EASY! We have it with garlic butter topped yeast rolls and a Caesar salad kit! Thank you for this recipe - it is in my permanent rotation twice a month!
I made according to recipe. Awfully bland. No flavor at all. It is not something I will be making again.
my grandkids wont eat anything with ricotta cheese or cottage cheese....my daughter made this, & it was great! (thats a big compliment from an old italian woman!)

We didn't have the correct cheese but added chunks of mozzarella through the dish and topped with a little more and grated cheese. Also used ground beef as didn't have the sausage. It was delicious and we will make again. I did use ziti pasta and made another with brown rice pasta elbows and it was also good.
it was great I left my alfredo out
This was as easy as 1-2-3. It was a hit with my family! And, the taste was absolutely delicious. I will be making it again.
Nasty....
